name: kbd
purpose: Keyboard shortcut shown as keycaps, from the same hotkey syntax as matchesHotkey ('Mod+Shift+K'). Mod is Command on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere; Apple modifiers show as symbols with their names for assistive technology.
whenToUse: Documenting a shortcut next to the command it triggers: menu items, tooltips, help pages.
Showing a key the user should press, such as Esc or Enter.
whenNotToUse: Code or command-line text: use a code element.
Interactive key remapping: Kbd only displays.
responsive: Inline keycaps that do not wrap within a shortcut; the combination wraps as a unit with surrounding text.
rtl: Key order follows the hotkey string in both directions (shortcuts are not mirrored).
theme: Keycap uses component tokens kbd-bg (color-surface-sunken), kbd-border-color (color-border-strong), kbd-radius (radius-sm); label color-text on kbd-bg is in the contrast gate. Monospace keycaps (font-family-mono). Forced-colors mode draws CanvasText keycap borders.
security: Key text is rendered with textContent; never parsed as HTML. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: Reads navigator.userAgent once per render when platform is auto. No persistence, network access, or telemetry.
limitations: One combination per instance; for a sequence (G then I) use one Kbd per step.
Platform detection uses the user-agent string (auto); set platform to override.
unsupported: Listening for key presses (use matchesHotkey from @absoluteui/utilities).
Rendering HTML or Nodes as key labels.
antiPatterns: Hard-coding 'Ctrl' for a shortcut that is Command on Apple platforms (use Mod).
Using a shortcut as the only way to reach a command.
